comparison: Both evaluate the screening methodology and findings (C38-C42). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of the multi-stage screening approach with statistical validation, while peer reviewers accepted the screening without criticism and found the data 'convincing.'

Both address AZD2858's effects on TopBP1 condensates and ATR/Chk1 signaling (C43, C49, C53). OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis of immunofluorescence and western blot data, while peer reviewers explicitly affirmed these findings as 'valuable' and noted the inhibition of TopBP1 condensates and Chk1 activation.

Both evaluate pathway specificity (C50-C52). OpenEval details the selective inhibition of ATR pathway over ATM pathway with statistical support, while Reviewer 2 explicitly confirmed 'AZD2858 therefore seems to selectively inhibit the Topbp1-ATR-Chk1 pathway without interfering with parallel branches of the DNA damage signalling system.'

Both evaluate GSK-3β independence (C54-C60, C93-C94). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of orthogonal experiments demonstrating GSK-3β is not involved, while Reviewer 2 explicitly validated this mechanism, noting that siRNA depletion and other GSK-3β inhibitors could not recapitulate the effect, suggesting 'a specific non-canonical effect of AZD2858.'

Both address disruption of TopBP1-TopBP1 and TopBP1-ATR interactions (C5, C61). OpenEval notes TurboID data support but suggests need for quantification and additional replicates, while peer reviewers acknowledged this mechanism without criticism as part of how 'disrupting TOPBP1 assembly inhibits the ATR/Chk1 signaling pathway.'

Both evaluate Xenopus egg extract chromatin data (C6, C62-C63, C102). OpenEval notes the data support increased chromatin accumulation but finds the origin activation interpretation speculative though appropriately qualified, while peer reviewers accepted the Xenopus extract data without criticism as part of 'convincing' evidence.

Both evaluate S-phase checkpoint inhibition (C66-C71). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of BrdU/PI flow cytometry and DNA fiber analysis with statistical validation, acknowledging heterogeneity, while Reviewer 2 explicitly confirmed these findings, noting that co-treatment 'partially reversed' replication suppression, 'consistent with the failure to activate ATR-Chk1 conferring a defect in replication checkpoint function.'

Both address compensatory post-replicative checkpoint (C72-C74). OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN due to lack of statistical significance (p=0.0654) and suggests need for additional experiments, while peer reviewers accepted this interpretation without raising concerns about the mechanistic model.

Both evaluate increased DNA damage from checkpoint abrogation (C75-C77). OpenEval details PFGE and western blot evidence with good reproducibility, while Reviewer 3 summarized this as a key finding that 'disrupting TOPBP1 assembly inhibits the ATR/Chk1 signaling pathway, leading to increased DNA damage and apoptosis.'

Both evaluate apoptosis induction (C7, C78-C81). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of multiple complementary assays with strong statistical significance, while Reviewer 2 explicitly confirmed that AZD2858 'can markedly enhance the cytotoxic and cytostatic effects of SN-38 and FOLFIRI through a combination of increased apoptosis and growth arrest.'

Both evaluate synergistic effects across cell lines and 3D cultures (C8, C82-C83, C85-C86, C89). OpenEval emphasizes extensive synergy matrix analyses and physiologically relevant 3D spheroid data, while Reviewer 2 noted the spheroid data 'sometimes considered to better represent tumor responses' and Reviewer 3 confirmed synergistic suppression of colorectal cancer cell growth.

Both address cancer cell selectivity (C84). OpenEval notes the data suggest selectivity but identifies limitations in replicates and variability, while Reviewer 2 found this 'an important point' but 'somewhat subsidiary to the main novelty,' suggesting the data are present but insufficient to fully establish therapeutic selectivity.

Both evaluate effects in drug-resistant cell lines (C87-C88, C99). OpenEval emphasizes the importance of synergy in SN-38-resistant lines for overcoming drug resistance, while Reviewer 3 noted effects occur 'even in drug-resistant colorectal cancer cell lines' as a key finding, with no reviewer questioning the resistance model data.

Both address TopBP1 condensates and drug resistance link (C35-C36, C99). OpenEval notes statistical support for differential TopBP1 foci between cell lines and citation support for resistance connection, while peer reviewers accepted this observation as part of the rationale for targeting TopBP1 condensates in resistant cells.

Both evaluate specificity controls with 53BP1 (C44-C46, C47). OpenEval notes well-demonstrated reduction in 53BP1 foci but unclear functional significance, while peer reviewers did not challenge these specificity controls, accepting them as demonstrating selectivity.

Both evaluate PML nuclear body specificity control (C47-C48). OpenEval notes appropriate statistical analysis demonstrating specificity for TopBP1 condensates over other membrane-less organelles, while peer reviewers accepted these data as controls without raising concerns.

OpenEval evaluated extensive background literature citations (C1-C3, C9-C34) as well-supported and appropriately grounding the study rationale. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressed these background claims.

OpenEval evaluated the integrative conclusion (C64) that AZD2858 disrupts TopBP1 condensates through multiple mechanisms as well-supported by collective evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressed this integrative claim.

OpenEval evaluated contextual literature citations (C90-C92, C95-C98, C100-C101, C104-C107, C110, C112-C114) as appropriately supporting the discussion. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressed these contextual citations.

OpenEval rated speculative hypotheses about potential advantages (C108-C109, C111) as UNCERTAIN, noting they lack direct experimental support and represent reasonable hypotheses for future work. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressed these speculative claims.
